title: Apple refreshes the iMac, entry-level MacBook Pro with the M6 chip
gist: Apple refreshes the iMac and entry-level 14-inch MacBook Pro with the M6 chip and N1 wireless chip, no design changes, starting at $1,499 and $1,999, with preorders October 28 and shipping November 6.

insights.claim: The iMac skipped the M5 and moves from the M4 to the M6, which Apple says offers up to 40 percent faster CPU, up to double graphics and nearly five times faster on-device AI versus the M4.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: On-device AI performance is Apple's headline upgrade metric.
insights.locator: Paragraphs beginning "It's a more substantial refresh"

insights.claim: The entry-level 14-inch MacBook Pro steps up from M5 with up to 30 percent faster graphics and up to double the Neural Engine performance.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: Incremental gen-over-gen gains for the MacBook Pro.

insights.claim: Both machines add the N1 wireless chip (Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6), the iMac gains up to 2.5Gb Ethernet, and there are no external design changes.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: Continued vertical integration into Apple silicon for connectivity.
insights.locator: Paragraph beginning "In addition to the M6 chip"

insights.claim: Pricing: iMac from $1,499 (two Thunderbolt ports) or $1,699 (four), MacBook Pro from $1,999; preorders start October 28 and ship November 6.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
